topics: 🧂 Primary and Secondary — bless the salted food and exempt the bread; when is bread ever secondary?
🍇 Fruits of Genosar — Rabbi Yoḥanan's feasts, King Yannai's sardines and pigeons, and the priests of Gufnit
🍞 After the Seven Species — Rabban Gamliel's three blessings vs. the Rabbis' one abridged blessing
📜 Me'ein Shalosh — the text of the abridged blessing and how to conclude it in Babylonia vs. Eretz Yisrael
💧 After Eggs, Vegetables, and Water — Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi, Rabbi Yitzḥak, and Rav Pappa
🥬 Food and Health — spleen, leeks, raw vegetables before four hours, cabbage, the turnip, and salted fish

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Primary Foods, the Seven Species, and What Comes After
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 44a–44b
overview.hebrewSource: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא עִיקָּר וְעִמּוֹ טְפֵלָה — מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָעִיקָּר וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵלָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Two mishnayot anchor this daf. The first sets the principle of primary and secondary foods: bless the primary and exempt the secondary — a rule the Gemara can only illustrate with the impossibly sweet fruits of Genosar, which leads into hyperbolic tales of Rabbi Yoḥanan's feasts and King Yannai's estates. The second mishna asks what blessing follows the fruits for which Eretz Yisrael is praised: Rabban Gamliel demands the full Grace after Meals, the Rabbis one abridged blessing, and Rabbi Akiva extends Grace even to a filling boiled vegetable. The Gemara supplies the text of the abridged blessing, debates its closing formula, then turns to what is said after eggs, vegetables, and water, and ends with a baraita on foods that heal and foods that harm.

slides.title: 🧂 When Is Bread Secondary to Salted Food?
slides.subtitle: The mishna's principle and the Gemara's unusual case

nodes.content: 📜 Mishna: they brought salted food first and bread with it — bless the salted food and exempt the bread, for the bread is secondary (טְפֵלָה)
❓ Is there any case where salted food is primary and bread secondary?

💡 Rav Aḥa son of Rav Avira in Rav Ashi's name: it was taught about those who eat fruits of Genosar — so sweet that salted food is eaten to cut the sweetness, and bread only accompanies the salted food

columns.label: Rav
columns.content: A meal without salt is not a meal

columns.label: Rabbi Yoḥanan
columns.content: A meal without a cooked dish with gravy (שְׂרִיף) is not a meal

callout.label: Genosar hyperbole:
callout.text: Rabba bar bar Ḥana: when a hundred of us followed Rabbi Yoḥanan to eat Genosar fruit, each brought him ten; when ten of us, each brought a hundred — and he swore he had tasted no sustenance. Rabbi Abbahu ate until a fly slid off his forehead; Rav Ami and Rav Asi until their hair fell out; Reish Lakish until he became confused and Rabbi Yehuda Nesia's men carried him home. Rav Dimi added King Yannai's city that supplied 600,000 bowls of sardines a week to the fig-cutters, and a tree yielding forty se'a of pigeons a month.

slides.title: 🍞 Grace After Grapes? Rabban Gamliel vs. the Rabbis
slides.subtitle: Mishna: after grapes, figs, and pomegranates — three blessings or one abridged blessing?

lines.speaker: R' Gamliel
lines.text: After the fruits for which the land is praised, recite the three blessings of Grace after Meals.

lines.speaker: The Rabbis
lines.text: One blessing abridged from the three (בְּרָכָה אַחַת מֵעֵין שָׁלֹשׁ).

lines.speaker: R' Gamliel
lines.text: My source: 'A land of wheat and barley, vines, figs and pomegranates…' (Deut. 8:8), 'a land in which you will eat bread…' (8:9), 'and you will eat and be satisfied and bless' (8:10). The fruits are inside the passage that commands blessing.

lines.speaker: The Rabbis
lines.text: The word 'land' in verse 9 interrupts the matter; 'you will eat and bless' refers only to the bread that follows it.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: But for Rabban Gamliel too, 'land' should interrupt! — No: for him that verse excludes one who chews raw wheat, which is not bread even for him.

lines.speaker: R' Akiva
lines.text: Even boiled vegetables, if they are one's sustenance, require three blessings. Rav Ashi: this means a cabbage stalk, which is filling.

callout.label: Two rules of thumb:
callout.text: Rabbi Ḥanina: anything of the five grains — 'Who creates kinds of nourishment' before, me'ein shalosh after. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: anything of the seven species — 'fruit of the tree' before, me'ein shalosh after.

slides.title: 📜 The Text of Me'ein Shalosh — and How to End It
slides.subtitle: Abaye asked Rav Dimi: what is the one blessing abridged from three?
slides.hebrewSource: עַל הָעֵץ וְעַל פְּרִי הָעֵץ, וְעַל תְּנוּבַת הַשָּׂדֶה, וְעַל אֶרֶץ חֶמְדָּה טוֹבָה וּרְחָבָה… רַחֵם ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֶּךָ, וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִירֶךָ… כִּי אַתָּה טוֹב וּמֵטִיב לַכֹּל
slides.label: The blessing:
slides.text: For tree fruit: 'For the tree and the fruit of the tree, and for the produce of the field, and for the desirable, good and spacious land You gave our ancestors to eat of its fruit and be satisfied with its goodness. Have compassion, Lord our God, on Israel Your people, on Jerusalem Your city, on Your Temple and Your altar. Rebuild Jerusalem Your holy city swiftly in our days, bring us up into it and gladden us in it, for You are good and do good to all.' For the five grains it opens 'For the nourishment and sustenance and for the produce of the field' and closes 'for the land and for the nourishment'. How does the fruit version close? One normally does not seal a blessing with two themes, yet Rav Dimi reported that Rav sealed the New Moon blessing 'Who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons'. So: Rav Ḥisda said 'for the land and for its fruits'; Rabbi Yoḥanan said 'for the land and for the fruits'. Rav Amram: no dispute — one is for us in Babylonia, one for them in Eretz Yisrael. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak objected: shall they eat and we bless for their land's fruit? Reverse it: Rav Ḥisda (in Babylonia) says 'the fruits'; Rabbi Yoḥanan (in Eretz Yisrael) says 'its fruits'.

callout.label: Takeaway:
callout.text: The closing of me'ein shalosh names the land, and whether one says 'its fruits' depends on whether one is eating the fruit of Eretz Yisrael itself.

slides.title: 💧 A Blessing Afterward? Eggs, Vegetables, Water
slides.subtitle: Three opinions, and what the mishna 'requires a blessing before but not after' comes to exclude
rows: Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi in Rav's name
Yes — שֶׁהַכֹּל before, בּוֹרֵא נְפָשׁוֹת after
Mitzvot — blessed before, not after; and for the Westerners who bless after removing tefillin: fragrances
Mar Zutra did not bless (like Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi); Rav Shimi bar Ashi did (like Rabbi Yitzḥak) — mnemonic: 'one like two, two like one'
Rav Ashi: 'when I remember, I act like all of them' and bless even after water
Rav Ashi's practice satisfies every opinion

callout.label: On eggs:
callout.text: Rabbi Yannai in Rabbi's name: anything the size of an egg — an egg is better than it. Rav Dimi: a lightly cooked egg beats six log of fine flour, a roasted egg beats four, and for a boiled egg anything egg-sized is inferior to it except meat.

slides.title: 🥬 The Sages' Food Baraita: Helpful, Harmful, Remedied
slides.subtitle: 'Cabbage for nourishment, beets for healing; woe to the house through which the turnip passes'

boxes.title: Beneficial
items: Spleen — good for the teeth (but bad for the intestines: chew it and spit it out)
Leeks — good for the intestines (but bad for the teeth: boil and swallow whole)
Any whole creature restores the soul — even tiny reed-fish (Rav Pappa)
What is near the vital organs restores the soul — the neck (Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov); Rava asked for meat 'from where the blessing is made'
Cabbage: even for nourishment, and also healing; six healers: cabbage, beets, chamomile water, honey, stomach, heret, liver

boxes.title: Harmful
items: Raw vegetables make one pale — Rabbi Yitzḥak: at the first meal after bloodletting
Raw vegetables before the fourth hour: forbidden to eat, and one who does may not be spoken to because of the smell — Mar Zutra declined while Ameimar and Rav Ashi ate
Anything undersized stunts growth — even a kid worth a zuz, unless it reached a quarter of its size (Rav Ḥisda)
A small salted fish, poorly roasted and without beer after it, can kill on the 7th, 17th, or 27th day (some say 23rd)

boxes.title: The turnip
items: Yet Rava told his servant: if you see a turnip in the market, don't ask what to eat with bread today
So when is it harmful? Abaye and Rav: without meat; Rava and Rabbi Yoḥanan: without wine; Shmuel: without wood, i.e. undercooked
Rav Pappa's wife broke it with eighty palm logs after cooking, since Rav Pappa's household lacked wine

callout.label: Closing thread:
callout.text: The mishna's 'one who drinks water for his thirst' is examined at the end of the daf: Rav Idi bar Avin says the phrase comes to exclude one who drinks for another reason.

summary.principle: A blessing follows the food that matters: the primary exempts the secondary, the seven species earn a blessing abridged from Grace, and after ordinary foods the Sages debate how far the duty to bless afterward reaches.

flowSteps.content: 🧂 Mishna: bless the primary and exempt the secondary — salted food over bread, for Genosar-fruit eaters
🍇 After grapes, figs, pomegranates: Rabban Gamliel — three blessings (Deut. 8:8–10); Rabbis — me'ein shalosh ('land' interrupts); Rabbi Akiva — even a cabbage stalk gets three
📜 Text of me'ein shalosh; closing 'for the land and for the fruits' in Babylonia, 'its fruits' in Eretz Yisrael (Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's reversal)

columns.content: 💧 After-blessing: eggs/meat yes; vegetables (Rabbi Yitzḥak); water (Rav Pappa); mishna excludes mitzvot or fragrances
🥬 Baraita: spleen, leeks, raw greens before four hours, cabbage, beets, turnip with meat or wine, salted fish

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rav Ashi's rule of practice — when in doubt about an after-blessing, bless 'in accordance with all of them'

quiz.q: In what situation does the Gemara say the mishna's rule 'bless the salted food and exempt the bread' applies?
o: At any meal where fish is served
For those eating the very sweet fruits of Genosar, who take salted food to cut the sweetness and bread only alongside it
On Shabbat, when salted fish is the main course
When one has no bread of his own
quiz.e: Rav Aḥa son of Rav Avira in Rav Ashi's name: the mishna was taught about eaters of Genosar fruit, where the salted food is primary and the bread secondary to it.

quiz.q: What is Rabban Gamliel's source for requiring the three blessings of Grace after the seven species?
o: 'Let every soul praise the Lord' (Psalms 150:6)
The seven species are mentioned in Deuteronomy 8:8, in the same passage as 'you will eat and be satisfied and bless' (8:10)
A tradition from Moses at Sinai
The fruits of Eretz Yisrael are as filling as bread
quiz.e: Rabban Gamliel reads the praise of the land's fruits (Deut. 8:8) together with the command to bless after eating (8:10). The Rabbis answer that the word 'land' in 8:9 interrupts, so the command refers only to bread.

quiz.q: After Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's reversal, which closing does one in Babylonia say for me'ein shalosh over fruit?
o: 'For the land and for its fruits'
'For the land and for the fruits'
'For the land and for the nourishment'
'Who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons'
quiz.e: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak objected that Babylonians cannot bless 'its fruits' while Eretz Yisrael eats them. So Rav Ḥisda, in Babylonia, says 'the fruits', and Rabbi Yoḥanan, in Eretz Yisrael, says 'its fruits'.

quiz.q: According to the Gemara, what does the mishna 'some things need a blessing before but not after' exclude according to Rav Pappa, who blesses even after water?
o: Vegetables
Water
Mitzvot, which get a blessing before but not after (and, for those who bless after tefillin, fragrances)
Eggs and meat
quiz.e: For Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi the mishna excludes vegetables; for Rabbi Yitzḥak, water; for Rav Pappa it must exclude mitzvot — or fragrances, for the Westerners who bless after removing tefillin.

quiz.q: Why did Mar Zutra refuse raw vegetables before the fourth hour while Ameimar and Rav Ashi ate them?
o: He was fasting that day
He held like Rabbi Yitzḥak's other statement that eating raw vegetables before four hours is itself forbidden
He believed vegetables require a blessing afterward
He was concerned they were undersized and would stunt growth
quiz.e: When they pointed out that Rabbi Yitzḥak's rule was only that one may not speak with such an eater, yet Mar Zutra was speaking with them, he replied that he followed Rabbi Yitzḥak's other ruling: it is forbidden to eat raw vegetables before four hours.
